summary: Impersonal I.1 retains 3sg.m predicate shape with l-experiencer, including independent hiye or ono; m- marks stimulus. Avoid calling the l-suffix an agent in these emotional predicates.
The inherited ruḥo plus ʕal pattern (I.2, LB154) remains numbered separately. Bare feminine adversity at 99/84 is grouped with I.3, without reconstructing a ruḥo noun.
III pressure targets take ʕal, while heart can be subject in its Detransitive. Existing III examples at 52/39,69/61,75/12,76/20 and84/7 are not new attestations.
New -wa boxes distinguish earlier constricted breathing (Preterit-wa) from continuing aversion (Infectum-wa). Supplied German has no authority to insert a Turoyo can-verb or negation.
Does kʕuyaqqe have default singular experiencer for a collective, or contracted plural?
Does breath tightness at MAC NE Mor Barsaumo/4 express boredom, oppression or breathing difficulty? Confirm b hn spacing at115/131.
Does aversion merit 1b, or should the editors further widen sense1? It is supported by contextual contrasts, not the free rendering alone.
What does -la resume in III gmaʕəqla with smoke as masculine subject at76/20?
Breath as possessed subject, compared with l-suffixed impersonal distress and ruḥo plus ʕal experiencer.
Pursuer applying physical pressure shares the existing ʕal-target frame; no extra pursuit sense.
